claims.text: Increasing configurational entropy retards diffusion-driven phase separation in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Increasing configurational entropy retards chemical segregation in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Retarding phase separation and chemical segregation enhances structural and chemical stability.
AlCoFeNi can exhibit a single-phase microstructure at high temperature.
The cited single-phase AlCoFeNi state is nanostructured and chemically homogeneous.
Multi-element atomic arrangements produce lattice distortions that act as kinetic barriers.
Multi-element atomic arrangements produce interfacial pinning that acts as a kinetic barrier.
Higher configurational entropy raises the energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
A higher atomic-diffusion barrier induces sluggish diffusion kinetics.
Sluggish diffusion maintains a homogeneous microstructure by delaying phase transformations during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Sluggish diffusion maintains chemical homogeneity by delaying segregation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Changing alloy composition can alter phase stability and the onset or extent of phase decomposition under annealing.
Higher-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will show later phase separation than a lower-entropy baseline under identical thermal conditions.
Higher-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit less chemical segregation than a lower-entropy baseline.
Higher-configurational-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit less microstructural coarsening than a lower-entropy baseline.
The proposed kinetic stabilization applies below melting or other extreme-diffusion regimes where kinetics dominate stabilization.
Quantitative phase-transformation onset and rates may depend on grain size and processing history.
